title: Optane rebuilt from abundant elements: one-film sulfide self-selecting crosspoint
idea: 3D XPoint died on cost: roughly a dozen distinct films per deck (As-Ge-Se OTS selector, GST phase-change layer, carbon electrodes, W lines) made at tiny volume. Fix exactly that by collapsing selector plus storage into one As-free, Te-free sulfur-rich Sn-Al-S chalcogenide glass whose polarity-dependent threshold voltage is the bit (self-selecting memory, no melt-quench), between Mo lines, so a deck is three films.
why: Removes arsenic, germanium (China ~60%) and tellurium (copper-refining by-product) plus ~9 depositions per deck; no melting lifts endurance toward 1e10+ and cuts write energy; est. 40-50% lower cost per bit than Optane on cost and scarce-resource axes.

title: Z-RAM without SOI wafers: floating bodies over silicon-on-nothing voids
idea: Innovative Silicon's Z-RAM died because it needed SOI wafers (two Cz wafers per substrate via bonding) and lost sense margin on bulk. Form local empty-space voids under the array by hydrogen-anneal surface migration of deep trench lattices (silicon-on-nothing), then partially refill each void with doped poly as a buried back-gate plate so every floating body has a strong back gate to hold stored holes.
why: Capacitorless ~4F2 cell drops the 60-75:1 TiN/ZrO2 pillar (no Zr/Hf, no high-AR fluorocarbon etch) and avoids SOI's 2x Cz silicon and quartz-crucible use per substrate; ~1.5x density and ~50% less crystal silicon per bit.

title: Thyristor RAM fixed with delta-doped barriers that pin holding current
idea: T-RAM and Kilopass VLT died because the gated thyristor's holding current and standby leakage swung exponentially with temperature, forcing SOI and big guard-banding. Insert a planar-doped (delta-doped) triangular barrier in the p-base so a designed barrier height, not bulk diffusion, sets regeneration; this flattens holding current versus temperature and lets the vertical cell sit in plain bulk silicon with no germanium.
why: Capacitor- and nearly refresh-free 4F2 cell: no ZrO2/HfO2, no TiN pillars, no 60:1 capacitor etch gases; bulk instead of SOI halves crystal silicon per substrate; ~2x density and ~40% fewer high-AR etch steps per bit.

title: ETA-10 lesson: liquid-nitrogen-immersed DRAM pods that need no refresh
idea: ETA Systems' LN2-cooled supercomputer died on per-board cryostat logistics, frost and service cost, not physics. Fix exactly that with sealed rack-scale LN2 immersion tanks fed by an on-site air-separation reliquefier (closed loop, no venting); at 77 K DRAM leakage falls ~1e6x so refresh disappears, and new cells can use ~4x smaller capacitors (~20:1 aspect ratio, plain Al2O3/SiO2 dielectric).
why: Kills refresh (~46 fJ/bit, 16-33% of idle power, 10-20% bandwidth) and lets capacitors drop high-k Zr/Hf and 60-75:1 etching; coolant is nitrogen (78% of air) instead of Qatar-exposed helium; cooler, faster wires partially repay the cryo energy.

title: Ramtron FeRAM without lead or platinum: aluminum-boron-nitride ferroelectric capacitors
idea: PZT FeRAM died on lead, Pt/Ir electrodes, 600 C anneals and a failure to scale below ~130 nm. Replace PZT with wurtzite Al(1-x)B(x)N (ferroelectric near x~0.07-0.15), sputtered below 400 C onto TiN or Mo electrodes, as a 1T1C cell whose ~100+ uC/cm2 remanent polarization needs only a short ~3:1 cup instead of a 60-75:1 pillar, refreshed only on power-down.
why: Removes Pb, Pt, Ir and the hafnium of HZO; Al, B and N are effectively unlimited and U.S.-producible; nonvolatile so standby refresh vanishes; ~20x shallower capacitor etch. Endurance of nitride ferroelectrics is the open risk.

title: NRAM revived with chlorine-purified methane nanotubes: a metal-free carbon cell
idea: Nantero NRAM stalled largely because CNT fabrics carried Fe/Co/Ni catalyst residue that DRAM fabs refused, and supply was boutique. Grow nanotubes by methane pyrolysis on a floating catalyst (co-producing hydrogen), strip metals to sub-ppb by ~2,500 C chlorine-gas purification as used for nuclear graphite, then spin the fabric as a two-terminal van der Waals switch between TiN electrodes in a crosspoint.
why: Switching element is pure carbon from natural gas (no Hf, Ge, Te, Pt), and the by-product H2 offsets fab energy; NRAM's ns-class switching, >1e11 cycles and nonvolatility remove capacitor and refresh; 4F2 crosspoint per deck.

title: Zettacore's redox molecules reused as DRAM storage nodes, not nonvolatile bits
idea: Zettacore's porphyrin memory died chasing nonvolatile retention through a 400 C back-end. Use the molecules where retention is cheap: graft a multi-redox monolayer (ferrocene-porphyrin triads, 2-4 electrons per molecule at ~1e14 molecules/cm2) as the last step onto a short ~10:1 TiN cup, so faradaic charge (~30 uC/cm2) supplies the 5 fF-equivalent storage that today needs a 60-75:1 pillar.
why: Attacks the capacitor charge wall: ~6x shorter storage node, no ZrO2/HfO2 high-k, fewer fluorocarbon deep-etch steps; molecules are C, H, N, Fe; refresh already exists so molecular retention limits do not matter. Electron-transfer speed is the risk.

title: CCD memory resurrected for AI weight streaming, where serial access wins
idea: Fairchild and Intel CCD memories (1970s, up to 256 kb) died because serial access gave long latency versus random-access DRAM. AI inference streams weights and KV pages sequentially, so build loops of 1k-4k charge-transfer stages per bitline that burst at GHz rates into one sense amp; cells are contactless overlapping-gate wells with no capacitor stack and no per-cell tungsten contact.
why: No per-cell W plugs (tungsten ~80% China) and no high-AR capacitor; constant circulation is the refresh; periphery shrinks to one sense amp per thousands of bits (attacks the 49% periphery share); est. 2-3x bits per wafer for streaming tiers.

title: Qimonda's trench DRAM revived by metal-assisted chemical etching at 200:1
idea: Trench-capacitor DRAM (IBM, Infineon, Qimonda, IBM eDRAM) died when plasma RIE could not push silicon trenches past ~60-70:1, and Qimonda went bankrupt. Metal-assisted chemical etching sinks a patterned catalyst mesh into silicon in HF/H2O2 vapor with straight walls beyond 200:1; use a sacrificial non-gold catalyst followed by a verified metals strip, then line trenches with ALD TiN/Al2O3-TiO2/TiN.
why: Gives the AR ~115+ needed for >8 fF without high-power C4F8/SF6 plasma (high-GWP, PFAS-class gases); capacitor sits under the transistor so the array stays planar; ~2x capacitance or ~30% smaller cell at the same charge.

title: Forcefill revived: high-pressure aluminum extrusion replaces tungsten contact plugs
idea: Trikon's Forcefill pushed sputtered aluminum into vias with ~700 atm argon and died only because copper damascene took over logic wiring. DRAM still fills every contact and bitline plug with CVD tungsten from WF6; fill the plugs formed after the capacitor anneals with Al-Si-Cu by high-pressure extrusion over a thin TiN liner.
why: Removes tungsten (~80% China) and WF6 fluorine chemistry from back-end plugs; aluminum is abundant and smelted in North America; Al's lower resistivity in narrow plugs trims RC ~30%; argon pressure gas is plentiful.

title: 1970s molybdenum-gate MOSFETs revived as fluorine-free buried wordlines
idea: Mo-gate MOS of the 1970s was abandoned because molybdenum oxidized and etched badly next to polysilicon. A buried wordline entombs the metal: deposit Mo by ALD from MoO2Cl2 (chlorine, not fluorine) directly on a thin barrier, recess it, and seal it with SiN so oxidation never occurs.
why: Replaces TiN/W buried wordlines: Mo has lower narrow-line resistivity than W, the U.S. mines roughly a quarter of world Mo (Colorado) versus ~80% China for W, and WF6 is eliminated; ~20-30% lower wordline RC.

title: Rutile TiO2 capacitors templated on MoO2 instead of scarce ruthenium
idea: Rutile-TiO2 DRAM capacitors (k~80-100) died on Ru/RuO2 bottom electrodes, a South African PGM that is costly and hard to etch, plus leakage. Template rutile on MoO2, a conductive rutile-structure oxide formed by in-situ oxidation of a Mo electrode, and suppress leakage with Al doping and a sub-nm Al2O3 interlayer.
why: k~80 versus ~40 for ZrO2/Al2O3/ZrO2 hits the 'k~70' route through the charge wall, letting pillars drop from 60-75:1 to ~35:1; removes Zr/Hf and Ru; Ti, Mo, Al are abundant; ~40% less deep etch and deposition gas.

title: MRAM minus platinum and cobalt: tau-MnAl junctions with voltage writes
idea: MRAM lost the DRAM-replacement race (toggle MRAM density, STT write current) and its stacks lean on Pt, Ir, Ru, Co and Ta. Build perpendicular junctions from L10 tau-MnAl (high anisotropy, low damping) free and fixed layers around an MgO barrier, written by voltage-controlled-anisotropy pulses instead of current.
why: Removes PGMs and cobalt; Mn and Al have several independent supply regions; nonvolatile so refresh is gone; VCMA writes ~1-10 fJ/bit versus ~100 fJ for STT.

title: Quartz-free crystal pulling: cold-crucible Czochralski from failed electromagnetic casting
idea: Electromagnetic casting held molten silicon in a water-cooled segmented copper crucible by induction, with no quartz, but died because it only made multicrystalline solar ingots. Combine that cold crucible with seed pulling and a cusp magnetic field so 300 mm dislocation-free crystals grow with zero quartz contact, and add nitrogen doping for gettering since the crystal is now oxygen-poor.
why: Removes the Spruce Pine high-purity quartz crucible (>80% single site) from DRAM wafer supply; oxygen-free crystals avoid thermal donors; melt power rises ~30% but one consumable chokepoint disappears.

title: Canon ELTRAN porous splitting stops grinding away 96% of HBM wafers
idea: HBM core dies are ground from 775 um to ~30 um, wasting ~96% of each Cz wafer; Canon's ELTRAN (double porous-Si layer, water-jet split) died because SOI demand was small and Smart Cut won. Grow the DRAM device epi on sealed porous silicon, process and bond it into the stack, water-jet split, and re-polish the donor for 10-20 reuses.
why: Cuts Cz silicon, polysilicon and quartz-crucible use per HBM bit ~5-10x and eliminates grinding slurry and rinse water; softens the material side of the HBM 3x-area tax.

title: MAPPER's bankrupt multibeam e-beam reborn as DRAM tile character projection
idea: MAPPER Lithography (13,000 beamlets, bankrupt 2018) died on throughput for random logic. DRAM arrays are ~95% identical cells: give each beamlet a stencil aperture of a full 8x8-cell tile so one flash writes 64 cells, exposing fluorine-free metal-oxide or HSQ resist.
why: Displaces EUV (one supplier, ~1 MW per tool, tin plasma, hydrogen) on 5-7 critical array layers at ~1/5 the capex; PFAS photoacid generators eliminated; 64x flash multiplication brings throughput to production class.

title: Canon nanoimprint for DRAM: repair maps absorb defects, fluorine-free resist
idea: Nanoimprint stalled on particle-induced defects and template wear. DRAM already repairs defects with spare rows and columns: imprint capacitor-hole and storage-node layers in UV-cure acrylate resist with a non-fluorinated siloxane release layer, map imprint defects by fast inline e-beam inspection, fuse them to redundancy, and replicate cheap daughter templates from one e-beam master.
why: Replaces EUV or SAQP on 2-3 array layers; imprint uses ~1/10 the energy and capex of EUV; resist and release chemistry are PFAS-free; ~10-15% wafer cost cut.

title: Supercritical CO2 cleaning, abandoned in 2000s, revived for capacitor rinse-dry
idea: Supercritical CO2 wafer cleaning was abandoned on particle redeposition and slow high-pressure single-wafer chambers. Aim it at the one place it wins: replace the repeated wet clean and IPA dry of 60-75:1 pillars with SC-CO2 plus amine/alcohol cosolvent residue removal and stiction-free drying, recirculating >95% of CO2 captured from ammonia or ethanol plants.
why: Cleaning is a large share of a fab's ultrapure water; claim ~30% water cut on array steps and removal of pattern-collapse yield loss, which also permits taller, thinner pillars.

title: Adiabatic charge-recovery wordline drivers borrowed from failed reversible computing
idea: Adiabatic logic died in CPUs because multiphase power clocks and slow ramps cost speed. DRAM wordlines are big, slow (5-10 ns), ~3 V capacitive lines, ideal for it: ramp each subarray's wordline to VPP through a 4-8 step tank-capacitor ladder and return the charge to the tanks on precharge.
why: Wordline CV2 at ~3 V is stuck (voltage floor); N-step charging cuts dissipation ~1/N (>60% at 4 steps) and shrinks VPP charge pumps in the periphery; energy is the resource saved.

title: Sinclair's audio RAM revived: sell partially good DRAM with defect maps
idea: 1980s ZX Spectrums used half-defective 64k DRAM ('ARAM'), a market that vanished as yields rose. With HBM yields down 20-30%, sort dies with failed banks, burn a signed defect map into an eFuse page, and let accelerator memory controllers or CXL expanders skip dead banks for KV cache and activations.
why: Every scrapped die is sunk helium, quartz, tungsten, water and energy; recovering half the fallout lifts usable supply ~10-15% with zero new materials or capex.

title: Undo the helium reserve sell-off: a chip-grade helium strategic stock
idea: The U.S. sold its Federal Helium Reserve (completed 2024), so Qatar's 2026 outage hit fabs with no buffer. Re-create a fab-dedicated stock: require 80-90% recapture of chuck-backside and leak-check helium (membrane plus cryogenic recovery) and bank recovered surplus and U.S. field helium in the Cliffside storage under a strategic-stock lease.
why: Helium is small in mass but irreplaceable for wafer cooling; recapture plus a reserve gives multi-year cover against single-region outages that otherwise cost weeks of DRAM output.

title: U.S. Memories redone: take-or-pay offtake plus chokepoint-free bill of materials
idea: U.S. Memories Inc. (IBM, DEC, HP, Intel and others) died in 1990 when PC makers refused binding purchases once prices fell. Re-form it with 10-year take-or-pay contracts from hyperscalers, a price collar (floor and ceiling), and a charter requiring at least two non-chokepoint sources for every input (Mo for W, recaptured helium, non-Spruce-Pine crucibles).
why: The U.S. makes ~1-2% of DRAM; offtake de-risks a $15B+ fab while the material charter removes exposure to helium, quartz and tungsten shocks.

title: IBM MXT memory compression revived for KV caches with block-float codecs
idea: IBM's Memory eXpansion Technology (2000) compressed main memory ~2x but died on latency and poorly compressible general data. Put a fixed-ratio 2:1 codec for KV-cache and activation pages (shared-exponent block-float plus entropy coding) in the HBM base die or CXL controller, with fixed page frames so there is no fragmentation and decode is a few-ns pipeline.
why: AI tensors have low-entropy exponents; 1.5-2x effective capacity means 33-50% fewer DRAM wafers, and all their helium, quartz, tungsten and water, per served gigabyte.

title: Purdue's 1990s silicon-carbide DRAM rebuilt on EV-glut SiC wafers
idea: Purdue built 4H-SiC DRAM cells in the 1990s with retention of hours or longer at room temperature, killed by expensive, micropipe-riddled SiC wafers. EV power electronics has since driven 200 mm SiC to low defect density and falling prices; build a planar or trench 1T1C cell on 4H-SiC whose 3.3 eV bandgap makes junction and GIDL leakage negligible.
why: Refresh essentially eliminated (16-33% idle power, 10-20% bandwidth); SiC boules grow by sublimation in graphite crucibles, so no high-purity quartz; U.S. SiC capacity already exists; trades density (~28-40 nm rules) for energy and supply security.

title: Shuttered Gen-10 LCD fabs reborn as stacked oxide-TFT memory fabs
idea: Giant LCD fabs are closing (Sharp's Sakai panel line halted in 2024) because TV panels commoditized, stranding PECVD, sputter, stepper and wet lines. Convert one into a glass-memory fab: 3-6 stacked oxide-TFT gain-cell tiers per ~9 m2 Gen-10 sheet, singulated into memory slabs, with only the host interface on a small chiplet.
why: Capital: reuses a ~$5-10B sunk fab at cents on the dollar; no Cz silicon, quartz crucibles, helium-cooled chucks or EUV; ~10 GB/m2 per tier at 1.2 um gives ~300+ GB per sheet, competitive as a capacity tier if sub-um patterning lands.

title: Zinc-tin-oxide gain cells: indium- and gallium-free, fixing ZTO's display failure
idea: ZTO lost to IGZO in displays because it resisted wet etching selectively against source-drain metals and its bias-stress threshold drift shifted pixel gray levels. In a 2T gain cell on glass neither matters: pattern ZTO by chlorine dry etch, and since every cell is rewritten each refresh interval, threshold drift is erased; off-currents near 1e-19 A/um give seconds-to-minutes retention.
why: Removes gallium (China export controls since 2023) and indium from oxide memory; zinc and tin have diversified supply; long retention cuts refresh energy ~100x versus silicon DRAM.

title: Uni-Solar steel coils plus HP SAIL imprint for kilometer memory coils
idea: United Solar Ovonic (bankrupt 2012) ran roll-to-roll deposition on 2.5 km stainless coils, and HP's self-aligned imprint lithography encoded every mask level as heights in one 3D stamp with no overlay; both died on solar and display economics. Combine them: planarized, glass-insulated steel coil, oxide-TFT gain-cell memory deposited roll-to-roll, all levels patterned by one SAIL imprint roller and sequential etch-back.
why: Substrate ~$5-10/m2 versus >$1,000/m2 for silicon wafers; no Cz, quartz, helium chucks or EUV; one stamp replaces 4-6 masks; ~4 GB/m2 at 2 um, so cost wins only if processing stays under ~$15/m2.

title: Thinfilm's printed memory minus PFAS: croconic-acid ferroelectric crossbars on plastic
idea: Thin Film Electronics' printed memory used PVDF-TrFE, a PFAS-class fluoropolymer, and died at tens of bits per tag on low density and high-voltage switching. Use croconic acid (C5H2O5), a single-molecule organic ferroelectric with ~20 uC/cm2 room-temperature polarization, vapor-deposited below 150 C on PEN film and imprint-patterned into a crossbar with printed ZnO Schottky selectors.
why: Removes PFAS entirely; feedstock is C, H, O; low-temperature processing uses little energy; ferroelectric state needs no refresh. Targets an abundant cold-working-memory tier; switching speed and endurance are the physics risk.

title: Core memory rethreaded by lithography: microtoroids around through-glass vias
idea: Magnetic core memory died on hand-threading labor and millimeter cores, not on its materials (iron oxide ferrite and copper). On glass panels, laser-drill via arrays, electroplate copper X, Y and sense lines through them, and form 5-10 um ferrite or NiFe rings around each crossing by room-temperature aerosol deposition, writing by coincident current.
why: Only iron oxide, Zn/Mn/Ni, copper and glass: no chokepoint input; infinite endurance and nonvolatile, so no refresh; ~1 GB/m2 per layer at 10 um pitch, so best for rad-hard or infinite-write tiers unless rings shrink further.

title: Plated-wire memory reborn as drawn multimaterial fiber woven into crossbars
idea: Plated-wire memory put the storage film on a beryllium-copper wire substrate and died on per-wire plating cost and coarse pitch. Thermally draw a glass/polymer preform containing conductor, charge-storage sheath and semiconductor layers into kilometers of 20-50 um fiber (multimaterial fiber drawing), then weave orthogonal fibers so each warp-weft crossing is a cell.
why: No wafer, lithography or EUV: a $1-2M draw tower makes km of device per hour from grams of preform; removes beryllium; ~1-2 GB/m2 of fabric, stackable in layers.

title: Williams tube on glass: field-emitter arrays read and refresh charge dots
idea: The Williams tube stored bits as charge spots on a CRT face and died on drift, bulk and constant regeneration; Candescent's field-emission display died on vacuum spacers and panel cost. Fuse them: a thin vacuum-sealed glass panel where gated carbon or Mo emitter arrays address an opposing grid of dielectric charge dots, reading by secondary-emission current and regenerating each frame.
why: Cells contain no transistor, no Hf/Zr dielectric and no tungsten plug; periphery is the emitter row/column matrix; built from glass, carbon or Mo and oxide films on retired FED/plasma panel lines.

title: Bell Labs ferroelectric matrix fixed by co-fired ZnO varistor selectors
idea: 1950s Bell Labs barium-titanate matrix memory died on half-select disturb because BaTiO3 has no sharp switching threshold. Co-fire a multilayer ceramic stack on the MLCC process (hundreds of ~0.5 um layers) where each BaTiO3 cell sits in series with a ZnO varistor layer (nonlinearity >30) that blocks half-select voltages.
why: MLCC lines already make trillions of BaTiO3/nickel parts a year with no wafer, EUV or helium; Ba, Ti, Zn, Ni are abundant; ferroelectric storage is nonvolatile; density limited by printed electrode pitch, offset by layer count.

title: Capacitor-on-foil revived: giant-k barium titanate fired on nickel foil
idea: Fired capacitor-on-foil laminates for PCBs stalled on coarse patterning and lamination yield. Make the foil the memory substrate: fire a 300-500 nm BaTiO3 film (k~1,000-2,000) on nickel foil at ~900 C in reducing gas, then build oxide TFTs above it below 350 C, so each cell's capacitor is a flat ~1 um2 pad holding >10 fF (~30 fF/um2).
why: Solves the capacitor charge wall with k instead of AR 115: planar capacitors, no high-AR etch, no Hf/Zr; nickel foil is cheap; fire-first then TFT sequencing decouples thermal budgets.

title: Thin-film magnetic memory on glass, read by cobalt-free permalloy spin valves
idea: 1960s thin-film magnetic memories deposited permalloy dots on glass but died on tiny inductive read signals and bulky drivers. Keep the glass and the permalloy, but read each dot with a NiFe/Cu/NiFe pseudo-spin-valve (thick and thin NiFe layers of different coercivity, ~5% GMR) and write with on-glass stripline current selected by oxide TFTs.
why: Removes Co, Pt, Ir, Ru, Ta and MgO from magnetic memory stacks; Ni, Fe, Cu are diversified; nonvolatile with unlimited endurance, so no refresh; cheap m2 glass substrate.

title: Kovio's liquid-silicon ink revived as stacked polysilicon memory tiers on glass
idea: Kovio printed cyclopentasilane silicon ink for RFID and died because tiny printed tags could not beat wafer chips on cost per die. Memory is area-dominated: slot-die coat the ink over whole Gen-8 sheets, convert at ~400 C, flash-lamp crystallize to large-grain polysilicon, and stack poly-Si TFT memory tiers without vacuum CVD.
why: Silicon devices without Cz wafers or quartz crucibles; grams of silicon per m2 per tier; no PECVD/LPCVD vacuum energy; ~100 cm2/Vs poly-Si also makes on-glass periphery possible.

title: Cavendish MEMS memory fixed: contactless bistable buckled nanobeams on glass
idea: Cavendish Kinetics' MEMS memory pivoted to RF because contacting cantilevers stuck and wore out. Make the bit the buckling direction of a pre-stressed, doubly clamped SiN or amorphous-carbon nanobeam that never touches anything: a coincident row/column electrostatic pulse snaps it through, and a sense electrode ~50 nm away reads it capacitively.
why: No transistor, no Hf/Zr dielectric and zero leakage in the cell, so no refresh; non-contact flexures survive >1e15 cycles; ~10-100 ns snap-through for ~1 um beams; built from sputtered films on glass.

title: Anodized-aluminum nanopores as lithography-free capacitor molds on aluminum sheet
idea: Anodic-alumina nanopore MIM capacitors reached very high capacitance in university labs but never shipped because pore-ordering defects made single pores unreliable. Use the aluminum sheet as substrate: anodize self-ordered 30-60 nm pores 1-2 um deep, line with ALD TiN/Al2O3/TiN, and define each cell as a bundle of ~50-100 pores so defects average out, with oxide TFTs on the planarized alumina above.
why: 30-60:1 capacitor holes with no lithography, no EUV and no fluorocarbon plasma (oxalic-acid anodization at room temperature); ~100 fF/um2; aluminum is abundant and smelted in North America.

title: Graphene lacked a bandgap; MoS2 capacitorless gain cells grown on glass
idea: Graphene logic programs stalled because a zero bandgap gives no off-state. Monolayer MoS2 (1.8 eV, 0.7 nm) shows off-currents below 1e-18 A/um: grow it by MOCVD at <=450 C directly on display glass and build 2T gain cells where the read transistor's gate is the storage node.
why: Retention of seconds or more cuts refresh energy >100x; no capacitor, so no Hf/Zr and no deep etch; a monolayer uses ~3 mg MoS2 per m2, from diversified Mo supply.

title: Photostructurable glass revived: laser-written trench capacitors inside the substrate
idea: Photostructurable glasses (Foturan, APEX) died in MEMS because UV exposure gave coarse, rough features. Femtosecond laser-induced deep etching (one pulse train modifies a line that then etches ~100x faster) writes ~1 um wide, 20-50 um deep trenches into plain alkali-free display glass; line them with ALD TiN/Al2O3-TiO2/TiN so every TFT cell sits over its own in-glass trench capacitor.
why: The substrate becomes the capacitor: no plasma high-AR etch (no C4F8/SF6), no Hf/Zr, and picofarad-scale charge budgets let tiny, weak TFTs work; trenches are direct-written, maskless.

title: Solyndra-proof loan guarantees for non-silicon memory fabs, indexed to DRAM prices
idea: Solyndra died in 2011 when the incumbent's input (polysilicon) price collapsed, not because its glass-tube technology failed. Structure CHIPS/DOE loans for glass-, foil- or SiC-substrate memory fabs with repayments indexed to a DRAM contract-price index (pausing below a floor) and tranches tied to tools re-taskable to displays or power devices.
why: The 4x 2025-26 price spike will reverse; indexed debt keeps chokepoint-free capacity alive through the down-cycle, roughly halving expected default loss and protecting U.S. manufacturability gains.

title: Holtronic's lesson: Talbot self-imaging prints sub-micron memory arrays on panels
idea: Holtronic's total-internal-reflection holographic lithography died needing perfectly flat substrates and costly holograms for arbitrary patterns. Memory arrays are periodic: displacement Talbot lithography (a grating mask lit by collimated i-line light while the gap scans one Talbot period) prints focus-insensitive 200-400 nm hole and line arrays across warped Gen-8 glass, with ordinary panel steppers only for periphery.
why: Raises glass-panel memory density ~10-30x over 1.2 um panel steppers with no EUV or projection optics; the mask is a cheap grating; lamp energy only; fluorine-free i-line resists.

title: NASA's vacuum-channel transistor as a zero-leakage DRAM access switch
idea: NASA's nanoscale vacuum-channel transistor stalled because emitter tips eroded under continuous current. A DRAM access device conducts only nanoseconds per access, a duty cycle near 1e-6: form 50-100 nm sealed vacuum gaps with carbon or Mo tips on glass that connect a storage capacitor to the bitline by field emission only when the wordline gate field passes threshold.
why: Off-state current across a vacuum gap is essentially zero, so retention of hours and no refresh; no doped semiconductor or silicon wafer; materials are glass, carbon or Mo and SiO2.

title: All-zinc ferroelectric FETs on glass: wurtzite ZnMgO gate on ZnO
idea: 1T FeFETs die on the ferroelectric/semiconductor interface: traps, depolarization and a parasitic interlayer that eat retention and endurance. Wurtzite Zn(1-x)Mg(x)O has been reported ferroelectric and is lattice-matched to ZnO, so sputter a coherent ZnMgO gate on a ZnO channel on glass with no interfacial oxide, and run it as a nondestructive-read cell needing only seconds-to-days retention.
why: Zinc and magnesium are abundant and widely sourced (no Hf, In, Ga, Pb); 1T cell with nondestructive read removes the capacitor and the restore cost of destructive read; DRAM-class duty needs far less retention than flash-class FeFETs failed to deliver.

title: IBM racetrack fixed with grain-free amorphous iron-boron wires on glass
idea: IBM's racetrack memory stalled because domain walls pinned on edge roughness and grain boundaries, and stacks needed Pt/Co/Ni multilayers. Sputter amorphous Fe80B20 (metglas chemistry, no grains) nanowires on fusion-drawn display glass with sub-0.3 nm roughness, shift in-plane walls by spin-transfer current pulses, and read at one end of each wire.
why: Stores 10-100 bits per access device, cutting transistors and periphery per bit; no Co, Pt, Ir or Ru; Fe and B are abundant; nonvolatile, so no refresh; shift latency suits streaming tiers.

title: No working p-type oxide? Build glass memory periphery from n-only circuits
idea: Two decades of p-type oxide TFTs (SnO, Cu2O, NiO) failed to match n-type oxides in mobility or stability, blocking CMOS periphery on glass. Stop chasing p-type: design decoders, wordline drivers and sense amps in n-only pseudo-CMOS with capacitive bootstrapping and precharge-evaluate dynamic logic in the same ZTO layer as the array, sharing 3-4 masks.
why: Periphery is ~49% of a DRAM die; sharing the array's single oxide stack roughly halves mask count on glass and removes the per-tier silicon CMOS chiplet; dynamic-logic power is acceptable at memory duty cycles.

title: Embedded-substrate failures fixed: memory tiers deposited inside glass package cores
idea: Embedded dies and passives in organic substrates failed because one bad buried part scrapped an expensive package. As processors move to glass-core substrates, deposit 2-4 oxide-TFT memory tiers on the glass core panel before build-up, test them with built-in self-test and redundancy repair at panel level, and bin packages by working capacity so a bad tier downgrades, never scraps.
why: Puts gigabytes of DRAM-class memory 1-3 mm under the processor, cutting data movement from 3-4 pJ/bit toward ~0.5 pJ/bit, with no silicon wafer, TSVs or HBM area tax; the glass core is already paid for.
